note: paprium-fw build manifest, read by tools/fwbuild.py. One source tree, two targets: 'pocket' (RV32IM images for the Pocket's cart MCU) and 'host' (x86 executable, the 'ours' side of the chip-vs-ours audit harness, our comparison test harness, which is kept outside this tree). The pocket source list is in LINK ORDER: it is the order the 0.2.6 build linked in (bash glob of src/*.c, then lib/source/*.c, then crt0.S), and the order decides where every function lands. Object files keep the 0.2.6 names (<basename>.o) because the linker scripts select input sections by object name.

brain.note: The CPU MATE brain (a reverse-engineered emulation of the game's CPU partner) is linked from OUTSIDE this tree. buddy/zz_buddy_brain.c .incbin's these three files by bare name; fwbuild passes -Wa,-I<brain dir> for that one source and refuses to build when an md5 differs.

pocket.toolchain_note: xPack GNU RISC-V Embedded GCC 15.2.0-1 (the 0.2.6 toolchain). Another GCC gives other bytes.

test.note: debug aids ON (snapshots, UART printf): B Jam's rule for every test/development build

legacy54k.note: The 0.2.6 layout, byte for byte: IROM 54 KB (rom0 32 KB + 22 KB extension, 11:1 slice mux), brain at 0x5360-0xD2EB, WRAM 32 KB. The linker script is the one the shipped 0.2.6 build generated (md5 33532367 as generated), kept as a file; only its comments have changed since, the linker commands are the same.

pocket72k.note: 0.3.0 locked layout: IROM 72 KB (rom0 32 KB + one 40 KB extension, 2:1 select), brain hole 0x5360-0xD2EB unchanged, WRAM 48 KB (the 0.3.0 map). The linker script is generated by tools/mkld.py from the JSON.

s1.note: The s1 source set: the new 0.3.0 firmware ('new core, same game'), the board interface v1.0 (board/board.h, docs/BOARD_IFACE.md) and the new core, built apart from the 0.2.6 source set above so the milestone images never change. 'tools/fwbuild.py s1' (and 'all'): the host tests (MSYS2 gcc, run, exit 1 on a failure) and the RV32IM compile checks. Every s1 compile gets -DFW_S1=1 and -DBRD_CLK_HZ=<clk_hz>u, clk_hz = the layout's (docs/MCU_INTERFACE.md section 7: the one clock value; --clk-hz overrides it for the clock test). Layout 'clk_hz' values are the RTL's CLK_HZ (NTSC); the 0.2.6 source set does not use them.
s1.layouts_note: layouts only the s1 source set builds at (a variant's "layout"; tools/fwbuild.py layout_cfg): pocket88k, the 88 KB IROM chosen for the FPGA fit of the s5 images (B Jam's decision of 2026-10-21), for the s5 variants (the test benches' images and the size report; no bitstream carries it yet)

pocket88k.note: IROM 88 KB (rom0 32 KB + a 56 KB extension), brain hole unchanged, WRAM 48 KB; generated by tools/mkld.py from the JSON

brain.note: The s1 source set links its OWN brain pin: the 0.2.6 brain with a cycle-counter fix (2026-10-13: nine addi immediates of the brain's counter moved to their structural twins, so c_hat equals the original's cycles with three player slots and in the Arena; brain.bin 1b64e14d -> b9a76592, same size and place; cf.bin and rodata.bin unchanged). The 0.2.6 source sets keep the top-level 'brain' pin (milestone 1 rebuilds shipped 0.2.6 byte for byte). The directory comes from PAPRIUM_BRAIN_DIR_S1 or paths.local.json 'brain_dir_s1' (tools/fwbuild.py); the files live outside this tree, like the 0.2.6 brain's, and are rebuilt by the fix's own recipe (not in this tree).

pocket.note: The s1 Pocket image (the new firmware's skeleton): own crt0 and trap entry, the board boot, the scheduler (core/sched) with weak hook defaults until the real code lands, and the brain bytes at their fixed addresses (the layout locks them). Object names stay <basename>.o, as the linker script selects by them. Variants: test and release as the 0.2.6 set; probe = test + the scheduler probe (tests/s1/sched_probe.c) that tests/equiv/fuzz_sched.py drives; probe_bug_* = the probe with one planted scheduler bug each (the fuzz test must fail on every one).
pocket.full_note: From 2026-10-11 the test and release variants add the full s1 set (variant_sources 'test' / 'release'): our version of the chip's dispatcher, status layer, job queue and event post (core/dispatch), app init and the boot page (core/boot), the register accessor (board/pocket/s1_freg.c), the 0.2.6 bodies re-hosted (interim/s1) over the moved 0.2.6 modules (legacy/026/mame.c, interim/album: FW_S1 guards only, compiled without -Wextra: no_extra). interim/s1 is first on the include path: its appmain.h replaces the 0.2.6 one for those files. The probe variants keep the skeleton with their own hook definitions (S1_PROBE boot).

pocket.overlay_note: From 2026-10-22 (test build 4b): the WRAM boot overlay (board/pocket/boot/c4b.h): the first-boot unpack of the cart's sound bank, the cache check, the SFX bank copy and the bar, compiled and linked on its own for wram_upper (tools/fwbuild.py build_overlay; board/pocket/link/c4b_ovl.ld) for every image here but the scheduler probes, with the image's own defines (the planted bugs C4B_BUG reach it), and placed in the WRAM image (tools/mkimage.py --wram-blob). -Os: 14.8 KB of the 16 KB room (15,124 B) (-O2 does not fit, measured); -fsigned-char: the WavPack tiny decoder's own rule ('a char must default to signed'; RV32 chars are unsigned); no gp and no small data (crt0's gp is the main image's); WVPK_OVERLAY puts the decoder's context and sample buffer at the stack floor (IBSS_ATTR). stack_clear = the bytes the overlay's stack scratch must leave below the stack top.
